title: Phota says it can fix the shot without inventing a new face
friendlyTitle: A new iPhone app says it can improve a photo without changing the person
summary: TechCrunch reported on 12 November that Phota Labs, founded by former Adobe computational-photography engineers Cecilia Zhang and Zach Xia, launched a free iPhone app that restyles everyday photos. The founders say their identity model is meant to keep the person recognizable, unlike a general image tool that invents a face when the source is blurry. Edited images carry an invisible watermark. Android is planned. A freemium price is planned later. The company raised a $5.6 million seed round led by a16z last year.
friendlySummary: On 12 November, TechCrunch reported that Phota Labs launched a free iPhone app. The founders used to work on photo tools at Adobe. whyItMatters: The useful test is whether the person in the picture is still the person. That claim comes from the founders, via TechCrunch, not from an independent check. A watermark helps a platform mark the file as AI-edited. It does not tell the person you send it to. The app is free while they build a user base. If you need a record of what the camera actually saw, keep the original.
